title: Policy Iteration Is Not Strongly Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
abstract: arXiv:2609.40147v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We establish an exponential iteration lower bound in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted Markov decision processes, with at most two actions per state. This rules out strong polynomiality of Howard's policy iteration when the discount factor is part of the input and yields an exponential separation from the simplex method with Dantzig's pivoting rule, which is proved to be strongly polynomial on this class. Even when each reward is restricted to logarithmic bit length, we obtain a stretched-exponential iteration lower bound. The gap between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest gain across all states reveals a ``price'' of algorithmic anarchy.

translated_title: 策略迭代对于确定性马尔可夫决策过程并非强多项式：算法无政府状态的代价
translated_abstract: 我们针对每个状态至多有两个动作的确定性折扣马尔可夫决策过程，为Howard策略迭代建立了以状态数为变量的指数级迭代次数下界。这一结果排除了当折扣因子作为输入的一部分时Howard策略迭代的强多项式性，并与带Dantzig转动规则的单纯形法形成指数级分离——后者被证明在这类问题上具有强多项式性。即使将每个奖励限制为对数级比特长度，我们仍然得到了一个拉伸指数级的迭代次数下界。Howard那种去中心化、各状态同时进行的自私改进，与Dantzig在所有状态间协调选择增益最大的单一动作之间的差距，揭示了“算法无政府状态”的代价。
tldr: 本文证明Howard策略迭代在确定性折扣马尔可夫决策过程上具有指数级迭代下界因而并非强多项式，而带Dantzig规则的单纯形法在此类问题上却是强多项式的，这一差距揭示了“算法无政府状态”的代价。
